skepticNotes.text: The quote for e_958bed8b90bb67e2 is 'We will ship the fix in the Sep 24 release. I am on leave from today until Oct 2.' but the registry text for that event contains only the first sentence and no leave statement; the claim's quote cannot be verified against the cited item.

Claim says Lin Chen announced leave with no handoff and 'leaving the client ticket without an active owner from Sep 20', but the leave announcement (Sep 20) and the failure to hand off are separate facts; nothing in the record establishes ownership status before or during Sep 20, and the Jira thread shows Priya Nair active on MER-101 throughout, so 'from Sep 20' is an inference not supported by the cited item.

Claims '4.12 live ... before the client ticket was filed' and 'Meridian's symptom is a one-day offset since that deploy'. The record (e_3de27219e6d5246f, e_33710584a8d8ae86) does place deferred go-live before ticket creation, but the claim is typed 'commitment' and labeled with a status of n/a; also 'declared live before ticket filed' is partly restated from Jira text rather than independently shown. Minor mislabeling plus a causal 'since that deploy' beyond what e_9ebd247d5f5b10e5 asserts (it attributes the report to Meridian, not verified cause).

Claim asserts Priya Nair's Sep 24 follow-up 'went unanswered', but the only evidence of no reply is the absence of a reply record; there is no explicit statement that this message went unanswered (by contrast e_73e857d2281453cb says 'no reply'). Calling it unanswered is an inference from silence, not a sourced fact.

Quote says 'no reply to four messages' as of Oct 1, but the registry lists at least five Northwind client emails (Sep 18, Sep 24, Sep 27, Sep 28, Sep 29, Sep 30). The 'four messages' figure conflicts with the record count and is not reconciled; also the Sep 18 email concerns SUP-2231 and should be excluded.

Claim says 'third unanswered message' on Sep 29, but the registry shows at least two prior unanswered client emails (Sep 27, Sep 28) plus the Sep 24 message, making the 'third' count ambiguous/contradicted.

Claim says client wrote Sep 27 'with no reply in the records', but the prior client message e_c430a56b45a8656c also has no reply record, and the Sep 27 text does not itself contain a 'no reply' assertion; labeling as a confirmed unanswered message is an inference from silence.

Claim says 'client had escalated internally over the silence' as of Sep 30, but the escalation email (e_dfa2b3a68bad7411) is dated Sep 30; also 'reply gap was not tracked by any owner' is an inference, not stated in e_44a0831730570fab. The Marcus question actually suggests he believed Northwind had been contacted, contradicting the 'no owner tracked replies' framing.

Root cause asserted with confidence 0.85 solely from the Jira merge note 'invoices now use a UTC conversion'. The merge note does not state that it caused the day-offset; that causal link rests only on Marcus Webb's later Slack assertion (e_4133bb30d78d5964), which is itself unverified. Claim presents the causal conclusion as established.

Same as claim 2: combines the Jira merge note with Marcus's attributed cause and labels the result 'root_cause' kept at 0.9 confidence, though no technical verification (e.g., code review, test reproduction of the off-by-one before/after 4.12) is in the record.

Calls Marcus's resolution 'unilateral' and a 'reversal' of his own decision. The record shows he said 'keep MER-101 open until QA passes' then resolved it the next day — a contradiction in his own words — but 'unilateral' implies disagreement he ignored; Dana's pushback (e_74e730159ddbde9e) came after the resolution, so he had not been contradicted at the moment of resolving. Wording overstates.

Claim says 'the shipped release did not actually fix the defect'. QA text says 'still failing on the Sep 24 build' in test — a test environment, not necessarily production; the record does not confirm production behavior. Claim extrapolates test failure to shipped production state.

Claims 'QA showed the fix was not effective'. Dana's message says QA failing on the Sep 24 build in test; it does not state the fix was present in that build or that QA tested the fix. Unsupported leap.

Long gap between Sep 10 Jira intake and Sep 20 leave announcement: no record of engineering work on MER-101 between Sep 10 and Sep 23 (first Marcus causal statement). Also a 3-day gap Sep 27–30 before Marcus asks internally whether Northwind responded — despite the client's continued messages. The records are silent on any actual work performed to fix the defect before Sep 24.

No reply from anyone (Lin Chen, Marcus Webb, Dana Okoro) to any of Priya Nair's emails appears in the record. Yet Marcus on Sep 30 asks 'Has anyone heard back from Northwind?' — suggesting the internal team believed Northwind was the silent party. This is a silent/contradictory state: records show no outbound replies, but also no acknowledgement that the client was waiting.

Dana's pushback on Sep 26 gets no reply in the record. MER-101 stays resolved with no visible follow-up or re-open. The claim says 'no follow-up owner' but there is also no response to Dana — an unanswered question that the claim does not flag.

'Is the Sep 24 release out?' (Sep 24) is never answered in the record. The release is only announced internally in Slack on Sep 24 at 16:00, after the client asked at 04:15 — suggesting the release was not yet out when the client asked, and no reply told them. The claim does not note the unreleased-at-time-of-ask detail.

Client asked 'Please confirm what went out' on Sep 27; no reply in record. No record shows what actually shipped in the Sep 24 build or whether the invoice fix was in the deployed artifact — the exact question is unanswered.

Client asked for 'a date for the fix' on Sep 29; record shows no committed date ever provided. Claim notes the request, but records also do not show what fix, if any, was planned after the Sep 24 build failed QA.

Contractual SLA reference (e_0ddd4cf69d223644 'Meridian carries a contractual SLA on invoice accuracy') is never investigated: no claim identifies breach terms, notification obligations, or whether anyone internally acknowledged the SLA. This is an unexamined angle directly relevant to escalation severity.

Marcus's 'Sep 24 release is cut; invoice fix included' is the basis for the broken commitment chain, but no source shows what was actually deployed (build hash, changelog, deployment record). No deployment/release source was searched — only Jira, Slack, and email. The claim that the invoice fix was included rests solely on Marcus's assertion.

Lin Chen's email (e_958bed8b90bb67e2) sent the client promise and leave notice, but the record contains no internal handoff of any of Lin Chen's tickets or context. The 'no handoff' statement is only self-reported; no investigation of whether any other engineer had context for MER-87/MER-101 appears.

Claim 1 and 3 both cite the same event (e_4133bb30d78d5964) with different types (commitment vs root_cause) and modestly different confidences — internally consistent as to content but duplicated; the 'commitment' label for Marcus's causal statement is a misclassification, and no separate commitment record shows Marcus told the client (channel was internal Slack, not client email).

Claim states Marcus 'attributed' the cause and 'targeted' the fix, but that message was posted in the internal meridian-billing Slack, not to the client. No record shows the root cause was ever communicated to Northwind/Priya Nair. The investigation leaves this client-communication gap unflagged.

Claims Marcus 'decided on Sep 25' to keep MER-101 open. The record shows him saying 'Let us keep MER-101 open until QA passes' — a proposal ('let us'), not necessarily a formal decision, five minutes after Dana's QA failure. Styling it as a 'decision' overstates a casual Slack remark.
